subject: Two simple equivalent (?)  log-normal regrssion models -> different results!

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Two simple equivalent (?)  log-normal regrssion models -> different results!
parts:
Hello,

I have two representation of the same regression

y = a * x + mu

y - a * x ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);

1) works but gives Warning
2) is stable but give a slightly wrong result

1)------------------------------------------------

data{
  int N;
  vector[N] y;
  real mu;
  real sigma;
  vector<lower=0>[N] x;
}
parameters{
  real<lower=0, upper=1> a;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[N] y_regressed_log;
  for(n in 1:N) y_regressed_log[n] = log(y[n]) + log1m((a*x[n]) ./ y[n]);
}
model{
y_regressed_log ~ normal(mu, sigma);
for(n in 1:N) target += -log(y[n]) - log1m((a*x[n]) ./ y[n]);
}

The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 4
                                                                                            count
Exception thrown at line 19: normal_log: Random variable[2] is nan, but must not be nan!       28
Exception thrown at line 19: normal_log: Random variable[1998] is nan, but must not be nan!     5
Exception thrown at line 19: normal_log: Random variable[21] is nan, but must not be nan!       4

2)-----------------------------------------------------

data{
  int N;
  vector[N] y;
  real log_mu;
  real log_sigma;
  vector<lower=0>[N] log_x;
}
parameters{
  real log_a;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[N] log_model;

  for(n in 1:N){
    vector[2] temp;
    temp[1] = log_a + log_x[n];
    temp[2] = log_mu;
    log_model[n] = log_sum_exp(temp);
  }
}
model{
y ~ lognormal(log_model, log_sigma);
}

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Any ides?

Thanks a lot!

I didn't follow along in detail, but I don't think your (2) is
a version of your (1), which would explain why they get different
answers. You need the Jacobian term to transform from normal
to lognormal parameterizations.

You can try to increase adapt_delta to avoid overflow or
underflow (which is where those warnings are coming from).

parts:
I have two representation of the same regression

y = a * x + mu

y - a * x ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);

1) works but gives Warning
2) is stable but give a slightly wrong result

Assuming y is distributed log-normal. (please specify more precisely),
then a*x + mu is on exp(a*x+mu) scale in 1), see:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log-normal_distribution
and in 2) -a*x is on log-scale whereas only mu is on exp(scale).

Is it correct to say, you want to do a log-normal regression in STAN
with only using a normal distribution and asking for the jacobian transformation
to do so, because you need some parameter restrictions which cannot
be done by using STAN lognormal function?

Andre
